content: Rabeprazole is a medication used to treat conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, and erosive esophagitis. It is also used to treat infections caused by Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) and other conditions where the stomach produces too much acid. Rabeprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Who should not use rabeprazole? Rabeprazole should not be used by individuals who are allergic to rabeprazole itself, Aciphex (a brand name for rabeprazole), other proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), or any ingredients in the specific rabeprazole product. Drug interactions Rabeprazole may interact with certain medications. Before starting rabeprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Specific medications that may interact with rabeprazole include methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, tacrolimus, and certain antiretroviral drugs like rilpivirine, nelfinavir, or saquinavir. Rabeprazole may also affect the absorption of other medications. Always discuss your full medication list with your healthcare provider to avoid potential interactions. Precautions before use Rabeprazole should only be taken if prescribed by a healthcare provider. Follow the prescribed dosage and do not share this medication with others, even if they have similar symptoms, as it may harm them. Keep rabeprazole out of reach of children. Do not chew, cut, or crush the tablets. Antacids may be taken alongside rabeprazole if needed. However, rabeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn, as it may take 1 to 4 days to take full effect. Health conditions to disclose Before using rabeprazole, inform your healthcare provider if you have any of the following conditions: Low blood potassium (hypokalemia) Low blood magnesium (hypomagnesemia) Low blood calcium (hypocalcemia) Liver problems Pregnancy and breastfeeding It is not known whether rabeprazole can harm an unborn baby or pass into breast milk. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your healthcare provider. They will determine whether rabeprazole is safe for you to use during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. How to take rabeprazole Rabeprazole can typically be taken with or without food. However, if you are using it to treat duodenal ulcers or H. pylori infections, it should be taken after a meal. It is unclear whether alcohol consumption affects rabeprazole, so consult your healthcare provider for guidance. Missed dose If you miss a dose of rabeprazole, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Overdose If you or someone else has taken too much rabeprazole, seek medical help immediately. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Common side effects The most common side effects of rabeprazole include: Pain Sore throat Gas Constipation Infection Headache (in children aged 12 to 17) Diarrhea (in children aged 12 to 17) Nausea and vomiting (in children aged 12 to 17) Stomach pain (in children aged 12 to 17) If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. There may be other side effects not listed here. Contact your healthcare provider if you suspect you are experiencing a side effect. Serious side effects Although less common, rabeprazole can cause serious side effects, including: 1. Kidney problems: Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis can occur at any time during treatment. If you notice a decrease in urine output or blood in your urine, contact your doctor immediately. 2. Antibiotic-associated diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can occur during treatment. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if these symptoms occur. 3. Severe skin reactions: Rabeprazole can cause life-threatening skin conditions such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that peels, flat red rashes, blisters on the skin or mucous membranes, and red, watery eyes. Stop taking rabeprazole and seek emergency medical attention if these symptoms develop. 4. Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS): This rare allergic reaction can affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Stop taking rabeprazole and seek immediate medical attention if these symptoms occur. 5. Lupus: Rabeprazole may cause or worsen lupus, an autoimmune disorder. Symptoms include new or worsening joint pain or a rash on the arms or cheeks. Inform your healthcare provider if these symptoms develop. 6. Vitamin B12 deficiency: Long-term use of rabeprazole (3 years or more) may reduce vitamin B12 absorption, leading to deficiency. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling/numbness in the hands or feet. Contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. 7. Low magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia): Prolonged use of rabeprazole or concurrent use with other medications that lower magnesium can lead to serious complications, such as seizures or heart rhythm problems. Symptoms include changes in heart rate, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. Stop taking rabeprazole and contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. 8. Bone loss and fractures: Long-term use of rabeprazole, especially in older adults or at high doses, may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures. 9. Severe allergic reactions: Symptoms include difficulty breathing, wheezing, rapid heartbeat, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, trouble swallowing, itching, rash, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or fainting. Stop taking rabeprazole and seek emergency medical attention if these symptoms occur. Storage Store rabeprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). How rabeprazole is supplied Rabeprazole is available as delayed-release oral tablets, typically in a 20 mg dosage form, under the brand name Aciphex or as a generic equivalent. If you have any concerns or questions about rabeprazole, consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice.
